AWS's name for its version of the Azure Portal
A Python library equivalent to Boto3 with no declarative features
AWS's native Infrastructure as Code service, built into the platform, using YAML or JSON templates

questions.q: In the template `Type: AWS::S3::Bucket`, what role does `AWS::S3::Bucket` play?
options: It's the resource type — a fixed identifier CloudFormation uses to know what kind of resource to create, similar to Bicep's resource type strings
It's the name CloudFormation will assign to the AWS account
It only works if the bucket already exists
It's an optional comment with no functional effect
questions.explain: Resource type strings like AWS::S3::Bucket tell CloudFormation exactly what kind of resource to manage, the same role Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts plays in Bicep.

questions.q: How does cleaning up resources differ between a CloudFormation stack and a Chapter 3 Boto3 script?
options: Both approaches clean up resources identically
CloudFormation stacks cannot be deleted once created
A Boto3 script always deletes its own resources automatically on exit
Deleting the stack tears down every resource it owns automatically, in order; a script has no such concept and requires remembering what it created
questions.explain: A stack bundles ownership of every resource it created, so deletion is a single reliable operation — a script has no built-in equivalent.

questions.q: Which command is AWS CloudFormation's real, built-in equivalent to Azure's az deployment group what-if for checking drift?
options: aws s3 check-drift
aws cloudformation what-if
aws cloudformation detect-stack-drift
boto3.detect_drift()
questions.explain: aws cloudformation detect-stack-drift compares a stack's live resources against its last deployed template and reports differences.
